title: U.S. Senate · Virginia

context.text: The Democratic primary was canceled and incumbent Mark Warner advanced unopposed. Bert Mizusawa won the Republican primary on August 4, 2026 with 51.5% of the vote, defeating David Williams (28.9%) and Kim Farington (19.6%).
Independent candidate Mark Moran withdrew from the general election and is not on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot.

summary.text: Mark Warner is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Senator from Virginia, first elected in 2008 and previously Governor of Virginia from 2002 to 2006. Before politics he was a telecommunications entrepreneur who co-founded the company that became Nextel. He is running for re-election, citing work on infrastructure investment, domestic manufacturing, health care costs, and his role on the Senate Intelligence Committee.

background.text: Born in Indianapolis, Indiana, in 1954. According to his Senate office, he is the son of a Marine who fought at Iwo Jima, grew up in a family that moved often, and was the first person in his family to graduate from college.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from George Washington University (his Senate biography says he graduated as valedictorian) and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 1980.
Worked as a staffer for Sen. Chris Dodd and served as chair of the Virginia Democratic Party.

Co-founded the company that became the wireless carrier Nextel. According to his Senate biography, he spent more than 20 years as a technology entrepreneur and investor in start-up technology companies, and launched philanthropic initiatives including the Virginia Health Care Foundation.
Won the 2001 race for Governor of Virginia and served from 2002 to 2006, governing with a Republican-majority legislature.
Elected to the U.S. Senate in 2008 and took office in 2009; Ballotpedia lists his current term as ending in 2027. He won re-election in 2014 and 2020 (defeating Republican Daniel Gade in 2020).

Serves as Vice Chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and is a member of the Senate Finance, Banking, Budget, and Rules and Administration committees; has chaired the Intelligence Committee earlier in his Senate tenure.
According to his Senate office, he is married to Lisa; they have three daughters and two grandsons.

priorities.text: Says he has worked to strengthen America's economy and "spearheaded the largest infrastructure investments in half a century" and expanded Virginia's domestic manufacturing.
Cites work to lower health care costs for Virginia families.

Cites his work on the Senate Intelligence Committee, where he served as chairman in 2021-2022 and serves as vice chairman in the 119th Congress (2025-2026), as central to "protecting the highest levels of America's national security."

record.text: Serves on the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs (Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Securities, Insurance, and Investment); the Committee on Finance; the Committee on Rules and Administration; the Select Committee on Intelligence (Vice Chairman); and the Committee on the Budget in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Bert Mizusawa
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 51.5% of the vote

summary.text: Bert Mizusawa is a retired U.S. Army major general and the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Virginia. He served in the Army from 1979 to 2016 and held roles as Deputy Under Secretary of the Army and as a senior advisor to the CIA Director. He describes his campaign as centered on national security, defense spending, and enforcing the law uniformly.

background.text: Graduated from Kecoughtan High School and earned a bachelor's degree from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1979.

Earned a law degree from Harvard Law School in 1989 and a master's degree in public policy from the Harvard Kennedy School; served two appointments as a MacArthur Fellow in International Security at Harvard's Belfer Center.
Served in the U.S. Army from 1979 to 2016, retiring as a major general. He describes 41 years of service, including four combat tours.

Was awarded a Silver Star in 1984 for service in Korea, where, according to Ballotpedia, he commanded the Joint Security Force Company at Panmunjom and led a Soviet defector to safety across the Military Demarcation Line.

Career roles include Deputy Under Secretary of the Army, senior advisor to the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency, and work for the Chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee; describes service as a professional staff member in the U.S. Senate.
Ran for the Republican nomination in Virginia's 2nd Congressional District in 2010 and lost the primary.
Was named in March 2016 to Donald Trump's foreign policy advisory team and served on Trump's 2016-2017 presidential transition team.
Describes himself as a small business owner who shares seven children and four grandchildren with his wife Amy.

priorities.text: Says he will be an "authoritative voice on national security policy and efficient defense spending" as a combat veteran in the Senate.
priorities.quote: Will be av respected, authoritative voice on national security policy and efficient defense spending. Combat veteran in US Senate.

priorities.text: Says the country is "a nation of laws" that must "enforce the law uniformly."
priorities.quote: We are a nation of laws and must enforce the law uniformly

researchNotes: Neither candidate has documented positions on the fixed issue keys via a direct statement, vote, or questionnaire answer found in this research; positions are left empty rather than inferred from party. Bert Mizusawa's Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey text contains minor typos in the original source, reproduced verbatim in quotes. Biography gaps: Mark Warner's Senate biography pages were fetched; Bioguide could not be loaded (blocked), so Ballotpedia and his Senate office were used. Bert Mizusawa's own campaign site could not be loaded, so his biography relies on Ballotpedia, including his Candidate Connection survey; the 41-year service figure is his own description, while Ballotpedia dates his Army service 1979-2016.
